residual_risk: Dedup is keyed on the transcript_path string as recorded. Two rows naming the same file by different strings (one absolute, one relative) would still double-count; in practice one Stop-hook payload writes the identical absolute path onto the root and every node, so this cannot happen today.

The reported path (run record, worker log) is untouched on purpose: those are per-invocation numbers and a resumed session could legitimately report two of them. If a harness ever writes total_cost_usd onto a track's nodes — Claude Code's Stop payload carries none today, and Copilot's agentStop carries no cost — that would double-count again, as a separate bug from this one.

Which of a track's rows carries the session is collection order (task order, then attempt order). The totals and the per-profile split are unaffected — a track's nodes all share one profile — but nothing should be read as a per-task cost off a single row.

This is verified against synthetic run records and a synthetic transcript; no track has left a session on this board yet, because #125 (the Stop hook never sees KB_TASK under a claude --bg worker) means nothing on the default profiles records session_id or transcript_path at all. The fix is correct by construction and by test, but it has not yet been seen on live data.
verification: new unit test: three nodes naming one transcript plus a cold node — the reader is called once per distinct file, one row carries the usage, usage.turns is 200 not 400, attempts_shared_session 2, attempts_missing_cost 0
new format test: the rendered report says "(2 transcripts over 4 worker attempts)" and the shared-session line
new end-to-end test through the command: three issues whose rows name one real transcript on disk — hkb stats --json reports estimated_usd 0.084, sources.estimate 1, not three times it
the docs sample block was rendered through computeStats/formatStats, not written by hand

results.summary:
hkb stats now counts a track's one session once, however many nodes name its transcript.

The bug (src/stats.js): since #119 every node a claude-track runner claims in-session carries the runner's
session_id and transcript_path — the same file for the root and each node. priceOf read that transcript per
attempt row and summarizeSpend added each row's usage, so a track of five reported five times what it spent.

The fix is a reader that answers once per FILE instead of once per attempt row (transcriptOnce): the file is
opened once, the first row to name it carries its usage and its estimate, and every other row of that session
gets counted:false — no usage, no estimate, no turns (num_turns would have doubled the same way). Opening it
once is worth having on its own: a transcript is the largest thing hkb ever reads.

Those nodes are moved, not dropped. summarizeSpend gained spend.attempts_shared_session, and they are
deliberately NOT in attempts_missing_cost — an attempt whose tokens are counted on another row is not a hole
in the coverage, and the "the real total is higher" line must not fire for it. The report says so where the
total is read: the usage line becomes "(2 transcripts over 4 worker attempts)" and a line under it reads
"2 worker attempts ran inside a session another attempt carries — counted once, there, not once per node".

Deliberately scoped to the transcript, the one source a track shares. A row with a cost on the run record or
at the end of its worker log is priced exactly as before, and so is a cold node whose transcript nobody else
names — the key is transcript_path, so rows that name no file are asked and priced individually, as before.

docs/harnesses.md: "A track is one session, however many nodes it holds" described the double count as a
caveat pointing at this issue; it now describes the fix, with the sample block rendered through formatStats
rather than written by hand, and names attempts_shared_session for --json readers. Both profile tables say
"counted once" where they said "one transcript for the whole track". Nothing in README.md stated the caveat,
so it needed no change.

Draft PR #131.
